transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. I guess I'm just here because... I get pulled off track really easily. 

Like, I'll be working on something, like finishing a dashboard, and... I don't know, a Slack ping goes off, or I hear a song lyric, or just get some random idea for another project. And then I just completely lose the thread of what I was actually supposed to be doing. So... yeah. That's mainly it.

Can you tell me whether you've noticed this kind of distractibility for as long as you can remember, going back to childhood or school years, or is it something that started more recently as an adult?

Um... yeah, I guess it's been a while. Like, since I was little. 

I remember in elementary school, my teachers would always write notes on my report cards. Stuff about me, um, rushing through worksheets or not following directions. And... talking over people during group work. 

My parents actually had to sit with me while I did my homework. If they didn't, I'd just... wander off or start doing something else. So, yeah. It's not new.
Besides the distractibility, do you notice things like feeling restless, needing to move around, fidgeting, or blurting things out or interrupting others when you shouldn't?

Um... yeah, I guess I do that. The fidgeting, I mean. 

Like, if I'm in a portfolio review for class or something... I'm usually bouncing my leg. Or twisting my rings around. I don't really notice I'm doing it, honestly. Um... I might click my pen or just keep shifting in my chair. Usually I only realize I'm doing it when someone actually looks at me. So... yeah.
Do you find that you often interrupt others or blurt out answers/comments before someone has finished speaking, like in class discussions or conversations?

Um... yeah. I do that sometimes. 

Like... if my group is brainstorming for a project, I might just blurt out my idea before they're done talking. Or... I'll just start adding stuff to their Figma board while they're still explaining it. 

I guess I can come off kind of pushy when I do that. I don't mean to, I'm just... excited about the idea, I guess. But... yeah.

Would you say these issues with distractibility, fidgeting, and blurting out have caused real problems for you in more than one area of your life—like both at school/work and at home or in relationships?

Um... yeah, I guess so. 

I mean... I've lost a few small freelance contracts because of it. And... I ended up missing out on a portfolio competition. Just because people felt like they couldn't really rely on me to follow through cleanly on things. 

And... I guess it affects my relationships, too. Like... some of my friends and people I collaborate with are kind of hesitant to work with me now. They say they like my ideas, but... yeah. It causes some problems.

Have you ever gone through distinct periods—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and had racing thoughts, separate from how you feel most of the time?
Um... no. Not really. I mean... I don't think I've ever felt like that. Just... normal, I guess. I sleep okay. So... no.
Do you often find yourself feeling anxious, worried, or on edge much of the time, separate from these attention and focus issues?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I'm an anxious person, mostly. Just... normal worried about school stuff sometimes, but not all the time or anything. So... no.
Do you use any substances like caffeine, energy drinks, nicotine, or other recreational drugs regularly, and have you noticed any connection between that use and your concentration or impulsivity?

Um... no. I don't really do any of that. 

I mean... maybe a coffee sometimes, but... not a lot or anything. I don't use anything else. So... no, I haven't noticed any connection.
Have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, for two weeks or more at a time?
Um... no. Not really. I mean... I have okay days and bad days, like anyone, but... not for two weeks straight or anything. I still like doing the stuff I usually do. So... no.
